title: S3 Storage & Cost Report
description: Reports each bucket's size by storage class from CloudWatch metrics, with an approximate monthly cost for ranking. Read-only, and it does not list objects.

inputs.label: AWS region
inputs.help: EC2 resources are per-region. Cost Explorer is global but only answers in us-east-1.

nodes.label: Size every bucket from CloudWatch
nodes.value:
import json
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
import boto3
from botocore.exceptions import ClientError

# A step with no cloud integration bound reaches signing time and raises
# NoCredentialsError as a bare traceback. The agent would then file that
# traceback as an observation. Fail here instead, with a sentence that names
# what is missing and who fixes it.
_creds = boto3.session.Session().get_credentials()
if _creds is None:
    print(json.dumps({"error": "No AWS credentials reached this step. Bind an AWS cloud "
                               "integration to this automation under Cloud Integrations, "
                               "and make sure it is available to this project."}))
    raise SystemExit(1)

REGION = "{{Region}}"
session = boto3.session.Session(region_name=REGION)
s3 = session.client("s3")
cw = session.client("cloudwatch")

# S3 has no "size of bucket" API. CloudWatch publishes daily storage metrics
# instead, which is why this reads metrics rather than listing objects — a
# listing walk over a large bucket would take hours and cost money itself.
STORAGE_TYPES = [
    "StandardStorage", "StandardIAStorage", "OneZoneIAStorage",
    "GlacierInstantRetrievalStorage", "IntelligentTieringFAStorage",
]
end = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
start = end - timedelta(days=3)

out = {"region": REGION, "buckets": [], "errors": [],
       "note": "Sizes come from CloudWatch daily storage metrics and lag by up to 48 hours."}

try:
    buckets = s3.list_buckets().get("Buckets", [])
except ClientError as e:
    print(json.dumps({"error": "could not list buckets: " + str(e)}))
    raise SystemExit(1)

for b in buckets:
    name = b["Name"]
    entry = {"name": name, "bytesByClass": {}, "totalBytes": 0, "objects": None}
    for storage in STORAGE_TYPES:
        try:
            points = cw.get_metric_statistics(
                Namespace="AWS/S3", MetricName="BucketSizeBytes",
                Dimensions=[{"Name": "BucketName", "Value": name},
                            {"Name": "StorageType", "Value": storage}],
                StartTime=start, EndTime=end, Period=86400, Statistics=["Average"],
            ).get("Datapoints", [])
            if points:
                value = sorted(points, key=lambda p: p["Timestamp"])[-1]["Average"]
                entry["bytesByClass"][storage] = int(value)
                entry["totalBytes"] += int(value)
        except ClientError as e:
            out["errors"].append({"bucket": name, "metric": storage,
                                  "error": e.response["Error"]["Code"]})
    try:
        points = cw.get_metric_statistics(
            Namespace="AWS/S3", MetricName="NumberOfObjects",
            Dimensions=[{"Name": "BucketName", "Value": name},
                        {"Name": "StorageType", "Value": "AllStorageTypes"}],
            StartTime=start, EndTime=end, Period=86400, Statistics=["Average"],
        ).get("Datapoints", [])
        if points:
            entry["objects"] = int(sorted(points, key=lambda p: p["Timestamp"])[-1]["Average"])
    except ClientError:
        pass

    entry["totalGiB"] = round(entry["totalBytes"] / (1024 ** 3), 2)
    # Standard storage list price; other classes cost less. Ranking, not billing.
    entry["approxMonthlyUsd"] = round(entry["totalGiB"] * 0.023, 2)
    out["buckets"].append(entry)

out["buckets"].sort(key=lambda x: x["totalBytes"], reverse=True)
out["summary"] = {
    "buckets": len(out["buckets"]),
    "totalGiB": round(sum(x["totalGiB"] for x in out["buckets"]), 2),
    "approxMonthlyUsd": round(sum(x["approxMonthlyUsd"] for x in out["buckets"]), 2),
    "bucketsWithNoMetrics": sum(1 for x in out["buckets"] if x["totalBytes"] == 0),
}
print(json.dumps(out, indent=2))
